findings.title: contract-queries.ts CONTRACTS/TESTNET_CONTRACTS is a drifted second copy of the per-app contract registry; feeds wrong hashes to 4 server surfaces
findings.evidence: platform/host-app/lib/chain/contract-queries.ts:11-31 hardcodes per-app hashes that are PRE-migration and disagree with the drift-guarded single source apps/shared/constants/generated-miniapp-contracts.ts (built from manifests). Concrete drift: last-survivor mainnet cq=0xa7840a8d… vs gen=0x8e1e432e…; testnet cq=0x740671b1… vs gen=0x8e1e432e…; gasbox/fogplay mainnet cq=0xa7840a8d… vs gen 0xeb635b6e…/0x5d82339d…; redEnvelope mainnet cq=0x5f371cc5… vs gen 0x363c5de9…; selfLoan mainnet cq=0x942da575… vs gen 0x87f94598…. getFlagshipApps() (line 45) hands these stale hashes to: pages/api/miniapps/[appId]/live.ts:35-49, lib/miniapp-stats/service.ts:51-53, pages/api/cron/rollup-stats.ts:45-53 (upserts stale contract_hash into miniapp_stats), pages/api/activity/events.ts:71. The decode logic is also coupled to the dead PlatformGame kernel ABI via PLATFORM_GAME_CONTRACT_HASHES/isPlatformGameContract (lines 36-43, 195-219, 252-263) — getDoomsdayState calls getCountdownStatus(appId) (a kernel method) whenever network==='testnet' OR hash matches the old kernel, so even when the hash is incidentally right it calls a method the new standalone contracts don't have. Result: detail-page live stats + cron rollup query dead/wrong contracts → empty or wrong on-chain metrics.
findings.fix: Delete CONTRACTS/TESTNET_CONTRACTS and source getFlagshipApps() from the shared MINIAPP_CONTRACTS registry (import { MINIAPP_CONTRACTS } from apps/shared/constants/rpc — exactly the precedent already applied in lib/rpc-helpers.ts:9,33). Then rewrite the per-app decode helpers (getDoomsdayState/getDoomsdayPlatformStats/getCoinFlipState/getNeoGachaState) to the new standalone ABIs and remove the PLATFORM_GAME_CONTRACT_HASHES kernel branch + the network==='testnet' kernel shortcut. Extend the drift guard (deploy/scripts/lib/miniapp_contract_registry.test.mjs) to also assert getFlagshipApps()==generated registry so this class of drift fails CI.
findings.risk: Medium blast radius: changes hashes/ABIs used by 4 read-only server endpoints + a cron. Reversible (data is recomputed each call); no on-chain writes. Decode rewrite needs per-app verification against the deployed standalone contracts' getter signatures.

findings.title: 4 migrated apps (fogplay/gasbox/last-survivor/self-loan) still declare runtime.mode=platform with dead-kernel modules + old kernel hashes; resolveMiniAppRuntime mis-classifies them
findings.evidence: apps/{fogplay,gasbox,last-survivor,self-loan}/neo-manifest.json keep runtime.mode='platform' with modules[].operations pointing at dead PlatformGame methods (placeCoinFlipBet/createGachaMachine/startCountdownRound/createLoan) and — critically — modules[].networks[net].contract_hash set to the OLD kernel hashes with registered:true (e.g. fogplay/gasbox/last-survivor mainnet all = 0xa7840a8d…; old testnet 0x238488…/0x740671…/0xe23851…/0x39d458…). dice-game already has the correct target state runtime:{}. Because contract_hash is non-empty AND registered===true, the self-healing fallback in lib/miniapp-runtime.ts:253 ( (!contractHash||!registered) && manifestHash!==contractHash ) does NOT fire, so resolveMiniAppRuntime returns mode:'platform' with contractHash=the OLD kernel hash, writesEnabled=true (miniapp-runtime.ts:263-280). pages/miniapps/[id].tsx:606-611 then takes the platform branch and injectRuntimeAppIdParam adds a hidden kernel-style appId param to host operations. Practical user-facing harm is partially masked only because fogplay/last-survivor/self-loan ship no host operation_panel/operations and gasbox's fallback is a local prepareMiniAppOperation launcher — but the runtime is still mislabeled (wrong mode shown in UI, wrong contractHash carried, dead method maps live), and any host operation re-added for these apps would invoke the old kernel hash.
findings.fix: Set runtime to {} in all four manifests (match dice-game), then re-run the registry generator. The contracts field is already correct, so resolveMiniAppRuntime will fall through to the dedicated branch (miniapp-runtime.ts:283-291) using the manifest standalone hash. Independently, harden miniapp-runtime.ts:253 so a platform module whose contract_hash differs from manifest.contracts is treated as stale even when registered===true (defense in depth against future manifest staleness).
findings.risk: Low: manifest data change regenerated through the existing generator + drift guard; no contract redeploy. The runtime.ts hardening is a localized condition change — verify it doesn't break genuine shared-mode/platform apps that legitimately use a different contract_hash than contracts.

findings.title: MAINNET_CONTRACT_DOMAINS_BY_APP_ID hand-maintains domain data that also lives in manifests (latent single-source-of-truth duplication)
findings.evidence: lib/miniapp-runtime.ts:59-73 hardcodes a 13-entry appId→domain map. findings.fix: Drop the hardcoded map and derive the mainnet domain fallback from the manifest contracts/domains (or from buildExpectedMainnetContractDomain which already exists at line 185). If a curated override list must stay, generate it from manifests like generated-miniapp-contracts.ts and add it to the drift guard.

findings.title: Two divergent getMiniAppContractHash implementations with different return contracts
findings.evidence: apps/shared/constants/rpc.ts:213 getMiniAppContractHash returns '' for unknown apps; lib/rpc-helpers.ts:50 defines a second function of the same name returning null and using a different NeoNetwork type and env-var-driven network resolution (getTargetNetwork). components/MiniAppPlayfield.tsx:4 imports the host one; pages/api/edge/[endpoint].ts:7 imports the host one; the shared one is used elsewhere. Same name, different empty-value semantics ('' vs null) and different network defaulting invites subtle bugs (truthiness checks differ) and makes the codebase harder to reason about which registry/network logic applies.
findings.fix: Have lib/rpc-helpers.ts re-export or thin-wrap the shared getMiniAppContractHash (normalizing one empty sentinel) instead of redefining it, so there is one resolver and one empty-value contract. Keep the host-specific env-based network defaulting as a separate getTargetNetwork helper layered on top.
findings.risk: Low: both already delegate to MINIAPP_CONTRACTS; verify callers handle the unified empty sentinel ('' vs null).

findings.title: On-chain read paths never check invoke state===FAULT; reverts/wrong-ABI calls silently decode to zeros
findings.evidence: lib/chain/rpc-client.ts:74-81 invokeRead() returns the InvokeResult regardless of state. pages/api/rpc/neo.ts:131-148 forwards the upstream JSON verbatim with HTTP 200 whenever upstream.ok — a Neo invokefunction that FAULTs is a valid JSON-RPC result (state:"FAULT") with no top-level error, so it passes through as success. components/playarea/bridge/request-handler.ts:60-66 invokeBridgeRead only checks `!response.ok || payload?.error`, so a FAULT result is returned to the miniapp as a successful read. contract-queries.ts (getDoomsdayState:191, getCoinFlipState:248, mapFromResult:117, parseInteger:67) treats a missing/empty stack as 0n. Net effect: a contract that reverts, or a call to a method that doesn't exist on the contract, is indistinguishable from a real zero — the user sees plausible-but-false state (0 jackpot, 0 players, empty) and no error.
findings.fix: In rpc-client.ts invokeRead, after parsing, throw if result.state !== "HALT" (include result.exception). In invokeBridgeRead (request-handler.ts), after extracting payload.result, if it looks like an InvokeResult and state==="FAULT", throw new Error(result.exception || "contract read faulted") so the miniapp gets a real error instead of a fake success. The WIF write path already does exactly this (wif.ts:644,750) — mirror it on reads. Callers in contract-queries/shared-mode already wrap reads in try/catch returning safe defaults, so surfacing the throw is backward-compatible while letting genuine zeros be distinguished from faults via logging.
findings.risk: Low blast radius: read-only; callers already catch. Slight behavior change: previously-zero stats for faulting contracts now log/error instead of silently showing 0.

findings.title: Host live-stats query stale pre-migration contract hashes with dead-kernel decode for 6 migrated apps
findings.evidence: lib/chain/contract-queries.ts:11-31 CONTRACTS/TESTNET_CONTRACTS pin lastSurvivor/gasBox/fogPlay all to the old shared PlatformGame kernel 0xa7840a8d… (mainnet) / 0x740671b1… (testnet) and selfLoan to 0x942da575…/0x39d4584d…. The generated registry (apps/shared/constants/generated-miniapp-contracts.ts) has the real standalone contracts: last-survivor 0x8e1e432e…, gasbox 0xeb635b6e…, fogplay 0x5d82339d…, redenvelope 0x363c5de9…, self-loan 0x87f94598…. getFlagshipApps() (contract-queries.ts:45-61) feeds these stale hashes into getContractStats/getLiveStatus, called by pages/api/miniapps/[appId]/live.ts:49, pages/api/activity/events.ts:71, and pages/api/cron/rollup-stats.ts:53. Worse than just a stale hash: the decode logic (getDoomsdayState:191 calls getCountdownStatus(appId); getCoinFlipState:248 calls getCoinFlipBetLimits(appId)) is coupled to the OLD kernel ABI via PLATFORM_GAME_CONTRACT_HASHES (:36-43). The new standalone contracts don't expose those methods → every call FAULTs, and per the previous finding the fault is swallowed → detail/activity pages perpetually show 0 jackpot / 0 players for these flagship apps.
findings.fix: Stop hand-maintaining CONTRACTS/TESTNET_CONTRACTS; derive getFlagshipApps' contract hash from MINIAPP_CONTRACTS[network][appId] (the same drift-guarded registry rpc-helpers.ts already uses), and rewrite getDoomsdayState/getCoinFlipState/getSelfLoanState/etc. to the new standalone ABIs (or drop the platform-game branch entirely now that no app maps to those hashes). Delete PLATFORM_GAME_CONTRACT_HASHES and isPlatformGameContract once decode is updated. Verify decoded method names against each deployed contract's manifest.
findings.risk: Medium: touches stats decode for 6 apps; each app's ABI must be matched to its standalone contract. Read-only, but wrong method names would keep returning faults. Reversible.

findings.title: 4 migrated apps still declare runtime.modules pointing at dead kernel methods; cron lifecycle + writes-enabled gating use them
findings.evidence: apps/{fogplay,gasbox,last-survivor,self-loan}/neo-manifest.json keep runtime.mode="platform" with operations maps to DEAD methods (fogplay place_bet→placeCoinFlipBet, gasbox create_machine→createGachaMachine, last-survivor start_round→startCountdownRound/rollover→checkAndEndCountdownRound, self-loan create_loan→createLoan) and old kernel contract_hash 0xa7840a8d…. dice-game has runtime:null (the correct post-migration shape). lib/miniapp-lifecycle.ts:134-145 calls getPlatformRuntimeModules(app) and derives statusMethod/maintenanceMethod from runtimeModule.operations, then readCountdownLifecycleState (:199-208) invokes getCountdownStatus and buildCountdownLifecycleInvoke (:189-197) emits checkAndEndCountdownRound against the stale 0xa784… hash — both nonexistent on the new last-survivor contract, so the chain-monitor cron's countdown auto-recovery silently no-ops (faults swallowed). getPlatformRuntimeModules also drives writesEnabled/disabledReason (miniapp-runtime.ts:245-290), so host runtime gating is computed off a dead module.
findings.fix: Set runtime to {} (or remove runtime.modules) in the 4 manifests as dice-game already does, then regenerate the contract registry. The standalone contracts self-manage their lifecycle (permissionless settle/rollover baked into each app's own flow), so the kernel countdown cron target is obsolete — either drop last-survivor from the lifecycle scan or point it at the new contract's actual settle method. Add a test asserting no manifest references the removed kernel method names.
findings.risk: Low: removing dead runtime modules only stops faulting cron calls and corrects writes-gating. Confirm no other UI relies on the platform-runtime module presence for these apps.

findings.title: self-loan mainnet invoke recipe calls createLoan as a plain invoke without depositing NEO collateral
findings.evidence: lib/miniapp-invoke/recipes.ts:773-820 — the `${SELF_LOAN_APP_ID}:createLoan` recipe's mainnet branch (targetNetwork==="mainnet", :791) returns a single invocation `createLoan(borrower, neoAmount, ltvTier)` with NO deposit leg, whereas the testnet branch (:820-862) correctly does neoTransfer(collateral) deposit-then-act and calls createLoan(appId, borrower, tier). The standalone MiniAppSelfLoan is deposit-then-act (collateral NEO must arrive via OnNEP17Payment with memo "selfloan:collateral" before the loan method, per migration notes). targetHash on mainnet resolves to MINIAPP_CONTRACTS mainnet self-loan 0x87f94598…, but the mainnet call shape (no deposit, 3 positional args) does not match the deployed contract's borrow flow → the invoke will FAULT at preflight (WIF) or be rejected by the wallet, blocking mainnet self-loan create entirely.
findings.fix: Make the mainnet branch identical in shape to the testnet branch: deposit collateral NEO (and optional pool top-up) via neoTransfer with the collateral memo, then invoke the contract's actual loan method with (appId, borrower, tier). Remove the mainnet-specific neoAmount-as-arg path. Cross-check the deployed contract method name (createLoan vs borrow) against contracts manifest before finalizing.
findings.risk: Medium: changes a fund-moving mainnet invoke. Must verify against the live contract ABI; a wrong method/arg shape would still fault. Reversible.

findings.title: Embedded-bridge invoke reports 'submitted transaction' as success on txid alone — a FAULTing on-chain tx still shows success
findings.evidence: pages/miniapps/[id].tsx:382-394 handleEmbeddedWalletResult sets invokeFeedback type:"success" with the txid whenever HOST_WALLET_BRIDGE_RESULT fires. That event fires in use-embedded-wallet-bridge.ts:117-120 whenever buildEmbeddedWalletBridgeResultDetail produced a txid. For injected wallets (NeoLine/OneGate) the adapter returns a txid once the tx is relayed/accepted into the mempool — it is NOT proof the contract executed with state HALT. A reverting transaction (insufficient credit, guard failure) returns a txid, lands on-chain as a FAULT, and the user is told 'Embedded workspace submitted transaction: <txid>' with no follow-up. (The WIF lane preflights, but injected wallets do not surface the on-chain result here.)
findings.fix: After receiving a txid, poll getapplicationlog (rpc-client.ts:87 already exposes getApplicationLog) for that tx and only confirm success when executions[0].vmstate==="HALT"; show a 'pending → confirmed/failed' state instead of immediate success. At minimum reword the toast to 'transaction submitted (awaiting confirmation)'. The store already schedules a post-invoke balance refresh (store.ts:95-103) — hook the app-log poll into the same delay.
findings.risk: Low-medium: additive polling; needs a timeout/abort and graceful fallback if the log isn't indexed yet. Reversible.

findings.subsystem: platform/host-app robustness, error-handling, and fault-recovery (wallet bridge, dispatch convention, edge proxy, RPC failure handling, session/wallet restore, on-chain stats)
findings.title: Sensitive-op confirm prompt runs before wallet/network validation, and authenticate reports target-network magic for an unverified wallet
findings.evidence: use-embedded-wallet-bridge.ts:99-106 calls confirmSensitiveBridgeOperation (native window.confirm) for invoke/send/signMessage BEFORE handleEmbeddedWalletBridgeRequest → requireBridgeWallet runs (request-handler.ts:102). So a disconnected or wrong-network wallet still pops the approval dialog; only after the user approves does it error with 'Connect wallet…' / network mismatch. Separately, request-handler.ts:115-121 'authenticate' returns network: bridgeNetworkMagic(targetNetwork) (the app's target), not the wallet's actual network, and requireBridgeWallet for authenticate is called WITHOUT requireVerifiedNetwork — so when walletState.network is null (NEP-21 getNetwork failed), a miniapp is told it is authenticated on the target network even though the wallet's real network is unknown. (Fund-moving invoke/send do enforce requireVerifiedNetwork:103, so this is informational, not a fund risk.)
findings.fix: In use-embedded-wallet-bridge.ts, short-circuit with the wallet/network error (call requireBridgeWallet, or a lightweight connected/network check) before showing the confirm dialog so the user isn't asked to approve something that will immediately fail. In request-handler.ts authenticate, return the wallet's verified network (and omit/flag it when walletState.network is null) rather than the assumed target magic.
findings.risk: Low: improves ordering and truthfulness; verify no miniapp depends on authenticate always returning the target magic.

findings.title: Detail page polls two activity endpoints every 5s for data hidden behind a collapsed accordion (and a dead edge)
findings.evidence: platform/host-app/pages/miniapps/[id].tsx:556-570 calls useActivityFeed({ pollInterval: 5000, enabled: Boolean(app?.app_id), newsEnabled: ... && showNews }). The only consumers of `appActivities`/`liveNotifications` are MiniAppStatusBoard and DetailTabsSection, both rendered INSIDE the `<details className="focus-mode-reference">` accordion at [id].tsx:792-833 which has NO `open` attribute (collapsed by default). So every detail page fires /api/activity/events + /api/activity/transactions every 5s regardless of whether the user ever opens 'Reference and diagnostics'. Worse, /api/activity/events (pages/api/activity/events.ts:27 getEdgeFunctionsBaseUrl) proxies to the Morpheus edge, which per project memory is currently degraded/down — so this is a perpetual 5s loop of wasted (likely failing) requests on the most-visited authenticated page.
findings.fix: Track the accordion open state (controlled <details> via onToggle → useState detailsOpen) and pass `enabled: Boolean(app?.app_id) && detailsOpen` to useActivityFeed (keep `newsEnabled` gated to detailsOpen && showNews). The realtime notifications subscription is already gated by newsEnabled; aligning the REST poll the same way eliminates the hidden 5s fan-out. The MiniAppPlayfield live-stats poll (the actually-visible data) is separate and unaffected.
findings.risk: Low — purely gates an already-non-fatal background poll; data loads on first accordion open. Confirm the news tab still hydrates from SSR `notifications` prop (it does: liveNotifications falls back to SSR notifications at [id].tsx:573-574).

findings.subsystem: platform/host-app performance + UX (OS shell, detail page, polling, RPC fan-out, bundle weight)
findings.title: framer-motion is in the global _app bundle solely for a basic opacity/translate page transition
findings.evidence: platform/host-app/pages/_app.tsx:6 imports { AnimatePresence, MotionConfig, motion } from 'framer-motion' and wraps every route in <AnimatePresence mode="wait"><motion.main key={router.asPath} initial/animate/exit .../></AnimatePresence> (_app.tsx:81-92). Because this is in _app, framer-motion lands in the shared chunk loaded on EVERY route — verified in the build: .next/static/chunks/pages/_app.js contains 193 framer-motion references. The animation is only a 0.2s opacity + 8px y-translate, achievable with CSS. framer-motion core is ~30-50KB gzipped on the critical path for all 20+ routes. (optimizePackageImports lists framer-motion in next.config.js:102 but that only prunes named imports, it cannot remove the runtime when motion/AnimatePresence are actually rendered.)
findings.fix: Replace the motion.main page transition with a CSS keyframe (a `@keyframes page-enter { from { opacity:0; transform: translateY(8px) } }` applied via a class keyed off router.asPath, respecting prefers-reduced-motion to match the current MotionConfig reducedMotion="user"). This removes framer-motion from the global critical path. The developer page (pages/developer.tsx) can keep its own framer-motion usage as a route-scoped (code-split) import. Net: framer-motion drops off the shared first-load JS.
findings.risk: Low/medium — visual parity must be checked across routes; the exit animation (AnimatePresence mode="wait") is lost with pure CSS unless you accept enter-only transitions (acceptable for a route change). Reversible.

findings.subsystem: platform/host-app performance + UX (OS shell, detail page, polling, RPC fan-out, bundle weight)
findings.title: Navbar and ConnectButton subscribe to the whole wallet store, re-rendering the entire navbar on every 60s balance poll
findings.evidence: platform/host-app/components/layout/Navbar.tsx:51 `const { address: walletAddress } = useWalletStore();` and components/features/wallet/ConnectButton.tsx:47 `const wallet = useWalletStore();` both call the zustand hook with NO selector, so they subscribe to ALL state slices. The store's background poll (lib/wallet/store.ts:85 setInterval 60_000 → refreshBalance → set({ balance, network })) mutates state every 60s, and every wallet invoke schedules an extra refresh (store.ts:95-103). Each such update re-renders the full Navbar subtree (logo, nav links, search input, language switcher, NotificationDropdown) even though Navbar only reads `address`. The mounted navbar is on every page.
findings.fix: Use field selectors: in Navbar `const walletAddress = useWalletStore((s) => s.address);`. In ConnectButton, select only the fields the connected/disconnected branches read (connected, address, provider, balance, network, error, loading, restorePending, clearError, disconnect) via individual selectors or a shallow-equality selector (zustand `useShallow`). This scopes re-renders to actual field changes. The detail page already uses field selectors ([id].tsx:245-248), so the pattern exists in-repo.
findings.risk: Low — selector refactor; verify ConnectButton still reacts to all the fields its branches use. Reversible.

findings.subsystem: platform/host-app performance + UX (OS shell, detail page, polling, RPC fan-out, bundle weight)
findings.title: Wallet balance background poll is not visibility-gated, unlike the other host pollers
findings.evidence: lib/wallet/store.ts:82-88 startBalanceAutoRefresh sets a 60s setInterval that calls refreshBalance() unconditionally — no document.visibilityState check. By contrast hooks/useActivityFeed.ts:161-189 and components/MiniAppPlayfield.tsx:99-131 both explicitly pause polling while document.visibilityState === 'hidden' and refresh on visibilitychange. So a backgrounded tab keeps issuing a wallet dAPI getBalance every 60s forever, and the post-invoke refresh timer (store.ts:99) fires regardless of focus.
findings.fix: In startBalanceAutoRefresh, skip the refresh when document is hidden (`if (typeof document !== 'undefined' && document.visibilityState === 'hidden') return;` inside the interval callback) and add a visibilitychange listener that triggers one refresh when the tab becomes visible — mirroring useActivityFeed. Register/unregister the listener alongside start/stopBalanceAutoRefresh.
findings.risk: Low — wallet balance is also refreshed on tab-return and after every invoke, so gating background polls cannot make it stale while in use. Reversible.

findings.subsystem: platform/host-app performance + UX (OS shell, detail page, polling, RPC fan-out, bundle weight)
findings.title: council-governance live stats fan out up to 20 separate /api/rpc/neo-read POSTs every 15s poll
findings.evidence: components/playfield/MiniAppLiveStats.ts:448-516 (miniapp-council-governance) reads getProposalCount, then loops `for (let id = total; id >= total-limit+1 ...)` with limit=min(total,20) issuing 20 invokeRead calls (MiniAppLiveDataShared.ts:6-22 each is its own POST /api/rpc/neo-read → one upstream invokefunction). MiniAppPlayfield.tsx:108 re-runs loadContractData every 15s. So opening this app's detail page triggers ~21 RPC round-trips every 15s. /api/rpc/neo-read sets only s-maxage=10 CDN cache (neo-read.ts:11-16) and there is no client-side request coalescing, so the per-proposal reads are not deduped across polls. This is the single worst RPC fan-out in the playfield layer.
findings.fix: Two options: (1) Reduce cadence/scope — only re-read proposal details on the initial load and poll just getProposalCount (cheap) on the 15s interval, re-fetching details only when the count changes. (2) Add a server-side batched endpoint or use a JSON-RPC batch array against the gateway so the 20 reads collapse into one POST. Option (1) is lower-effort and removes ~20 round-trips per poll for the steady state.
findings.risk: Low — read-only; the displayed active/finalized counts may lag a proposal-status change by one count-poll, acceptable for a stats card. Reversible.

findings.subsystem: platform/host-app performance + UX (OS shell, detail page, polling, RPC fan-out, bundle weight)
findings.title: LiveChat polls /api/chat messages every 5s with no visibility gating
findings.evidence: components/features/chat/LiveChat.tsx:62-89 sets setInterval(fetchMessages, 5000) when the panel isOpen, but unlike the other host pollers (useActivityFeed, MiniAppPlayfield) it has no document.visibilityState check, so a backgrounded tab with the chat panel left open keeps fetching every 5s. It also `setLoading(true)` on every poll tick (line 68), which can cause a loading-flicker on each refresh in the chat UI.
findings.fix: Skip the fetch when document.visibilityState === 'hidden' and refresh on visibilitychange (reuse the pattern from useActivityFeed). Only set loading on the initial fetch (track an isInitial flag) so the 5s background refresh does not toggle the loading state.
findings.risk: Low — chat stays current while focused; reversible.

findings.title: Unused heavy dependencies (recharts, ethers) shipped in host-app and stale optimizePackageImports entry
findings.evidence: package.json lists recharts ^3.6.0 and ethers ^6.16.0 as runtime deps, but grep across components/pages/lib finds zero imports of either (only references are tests/none). next.config.js:102 still lists 'recharts' in experimental.optimizePackageImports even though nothing imports it. findings.subsystem: platform/host-app performance + UX (OS shell, detail page, polling, RPC fan-out, bundle weight)
findings.title: Detail page lacks a loading state for the action console while wallet/network resolves; only the playfield shows skeletons
findings.evidence: pages/miniapps/[id].tsx renders the action panel (aside, lines 836-953) immediately from SSR props, but the wallet connection state (walletConnected/walletNetwork) hydrates client-side from the persisted zustand store via restoreSession (store.ts:282-323, deferred past store creation per onRehydrateStorage). During that window actionConsoleStatusLabel computes to 'Wallet Required' / NetworkSafetyBadge shows an unsafe state ([id].tsx:662-688, 912-919) even for a user who has a persisted session that is about to silently reconnect. There is no 'restoring session…' affordance on the detail action panel (the ConnectButton has a resume chip, but the detail panel does not reflect restorePending).
findings.fix: Read `restorePending`/`loading` from the wallet store on the detail page and, while a persisted session is being restored, render a neutral 'Checking wallet…' state on the action console instead of the 'Wallet Required'/unsafe-network messaging, so a returning user is not briefly told to connect a wallet they already have.
findings.risk: Low — purely additive UI state; reversible.

findings.subsystem: apps-shared
findings.title: N3Index apiFetch uses raw fetch with no timeout — hangs the deposit-confirmation poller for every payment flow
findings.evidence: apps/shared/utils/n3index.ts:96-116 apiFetch does `const res = await fetch(url.toString())` with no AbortController/timeout. This backs getContractEvents → waitForTransactionStatus (n3index.ts:296-323), whose poll loop only checks `Date.now() >= deadline` BETWEEN iterations (line 320) — a single hung connection blocks inside `await getContractEvents(...)` forever, so the deadline is never reached. waitForTransactionStatus is the body of waitForDepositConfirmation (useContractInteraction.ts:87-100), called by ChainService.prepayAndInvoke (ChainService.ts:578) and invokeWithDirectPrepaidGas (useContractInteraction.ts:411) — i.e. the deposit-then-act path of EVERY migrated payment app, plus 4 apps call it directly. A stalled indexer freezes the whole withProcessing() write (ChainService.ts:289-300) with isProcessing stuck true. The codebase already has fetchWithTimeout (apps/shared/utils/fetch-timeout.ts) built for exactly this, and useEvents/wallet-sdk-composables.ts + EdgeClient.ts already use timeouts; n3index is the one transport that doesn't.
findings.fix: Route apiFetch in n3index.ts through fetchWithTimeout (import from ./fetch-timeout) with a sane per-request deadline (e.g. 10s). This bounds every getContractEvents/getAccount/etc. call and lets waitForTransactionStatus's poll deadline actually fire; a per-request timeout surfaces as a poll error that the existing `!reachable → unreachable` / deadline logic already handles, falling back to the fixed settle delay.
findings.risk: Low — additive timeout on an HTTP helper; existing callers already treat indexer errors as recoverable (unreachable/timeout). Pick a timeout (>= pollIntervalMs) so a normal slow response isn't aborted mid-poll.

findings.subsystem: apps-shared
findings.title: Stale runtime.modules in 4 migrated app manifests render host operation buttons that call DEAD kernel methods
findings.evidence: Confirmed seeded finding. apps/fogplay/neo-manifest.json, apps/gasbox/neo-manifest.json, apps/last-survivor/neo-manifest.json, apps/self-loan/neo-manifest.json all still declare runtime.mode="platform" with modules whose operations map to old PlatformGame/PlatformDeFi kernel methods — fogplay operations.place_bet="placeCoinFlipBet", gasbox create_machine="createGachaMachine", last-survivor start_round="startCountdownRound", self-loan create_loan="createLoan" — and pre-migration kernel hashes (e.g. all three games point neo-n3-mainnet contract_hash at 0xa7840a8d5404bbe297a00756a29cc267d6fa6cc7). These methods do not exist on the new standalone contracts (fogplay 0x5d82339d.../gasbox 0xeb635b6e.../last-survivor 0x8e1e432e.../self-loan 0x87f94598... per apps/shared/constants/generated-miniapp-contracts.ts). The host renders these as buttons: platform/host-app/components/features/miniapp/SharedRuntimePanel.tsx + lib/miniapp-runtime.ts consume runtime.modules; dice-game already has runtime:null (verified). Users clicking those buttons hit non-existent methods → faulted invocations.
findings.fix: Set runtime to {} (or remove it) in the four manifests, matching dice-game. Then re-run scripts/generate-miniapp-contract-registry.mjs so generated registries stay consistent. The migrated frontends already drive the contracts via ctx.services.chain, so the platform runtime panel is pure dead surface here.
findings.risk: Low/reversible — pure manifest data; the standalone PlayAreas don't depend on runtime.modules. Re-run the contract-registry drift guard (deploy/scripts/lib/miniapp_contract_registry.test.mjs) after.

findings.title: Host contract-queries.ts holds pre-migration kernel hashes + old-ABI decoders for lastSurvivor/gasBox/fogPlay
findings.evidence: Confirmed seeded finding (adjacent subsystem; apps/shared registry itself is correct). platform/host-app/lib/chain/contract-queries.ts:12-16 maps lastSurvivor/gasBox/fogPlay to 0xa7840a8d5404bbe297a00756a29cc267d6fa6cc7 (the old PlatformGame kernel) for mainnet, with PLATFORM_GAME_CONTRACT_HASHES (lines 36-42) and per-app decode cases (lines 297, 329-330, 351) coupled to the old-kernel ABI. findings.fix: In platform/host-app/lib/chain/contract-queries.ts, derive the per-app contract hash from the shared registry (MINIAPP_CONTRACTS / getMiniAppContractHash) instead of the hardcoded CONTRACTS/TESTNET_CONTRACTS entries, and rewrite the lastSurvivor/gasBox/fogPlay/redenvelope/selfLoan/platformAnchor decode cases to the new standalone ABIs (mirror each app's PlayArea read parsing). findings.subsystem: apps-shared
findings.title: TransferService.scaleAmount scales GAS with floating-point math, bypassing the canonical no-float amounts.ts
findings.evidence: apps/shared/services/TransferService.ts:152 returns `String(Math.round(parsed * TOKEN_CONSTANTS.GAS_MULTIPLIER))` where parsed=Number(amount). Verified precision loss: "99999999.99999999" GAS → 9999999999999998 (correct is ...9999), off by 1 base unit, and the error grows for larger amounts. This is exactly the float bug apps/shared/utils/amounts.ts (gasToBaseUnits) was promoted to eliminate ("the #1 correctness risk... the SINGLE scaling point... without floats") and which the 2026-06-04 audit already hit elsewhere (String(0.7/7)). It is currently latent: grep shows TransferService.transferGas/transferToken/prepayGas have ZERO app callers — it is a defined-but-unused public shared API. The risk is a future app adopting it and silently moving a wrong amount.
findings.fix: Replace scaleAmount's GAS branch with gasToBaseUnits(amount) from utils/amounts.ts (string-based bigint scaling) and the NEO branch with neoToInteger(amount); throw on a 0n result. This makes the public TransferService consistent with the helper every app already uses. If TransferService is intended to stay unused, consider removing it to shrink the public surface.
findings.risk: Low — internal scaling change to an unused method; gasToBaseUnits already validates/rejects malformed input. Behavior for valid sub-1e8-precision amounts is unchanged.

findings.subsystem: apps-shared
findings.title: PlatformServices.destroy() never disposes useContractInteraction timers (leak on unmount)
findings.evidence: ChainService wraps useContractInteraction() (ChainService.ts:177), which creates successTimer + waitTimers and exposes a dispose() that clears them (useContractInteraction.ts:160-168, 430-438). ChainService neither exposes nor calls interaction.dispose(). PlatformServices.destroy() (PlatformServices.ts:148-152) only calls lifecycle.unmount(), cache.destroy(), events.destroy() — never touches chain/interaction. MiniAppRoot.tsx:395 calls services.destroy() on unmount, so on every app teardown the interaction's pending timers (set during in-flight delay()/triggerSuccess()) leak. Bounded (timers self-clear in ~4s/3.5s) but real, and matters when users navigate rapidly across the 60 miniapps.
findings.fix: Add a dispose()/destroy() method to ChainService that calls this.interaction.dispose(), and call it from PlatformServices.destroy() (before events.destroy()). Optionally also clear ChainService-owned subscriptions if any are added later.
findings.risk: Low — pure cleanup wiring; dispose() is idempotent (clears timers and resets arrays).

findings.title: Host bundled definitions (public/miniapp-definitions/*.json) carry stale top-level operations + missing contracts → detail page renders dead/oracle-phantom action buttons
findings.evidence: platform/host-app/public/miniapp-definitions/{fogplay,self-loan,last-survivor,dice-game}.json carry stale top-level operations consumed by pages/miniapps/[id].tsx:582-611: fogplay=['fundGameCredit','fundOracleRequestFee','placeCoinFlipBet'] (placeCoinFlipBet dead on new ABI; fundOracleRequestFee is an oracle method but the manifest sets technologies.oracle.enabled=false — phantom button), self-loan=['createLoan','repayLoan','addCollateral','syncProfitAnchorVote'] (createLoan/repayLoan dead; new ABI uses borrow/repay), last-survivor=['fundGameCredit','buyCountdownKeys'] (buyCountdownKeys dead; new=buyKeys), dice-game=['fundGameCredit','fundOracleRequestFee','placeDiceBet'] (fundOracleRequestFee dead — dice-game manifest has no oracle, its operation_panel only defines fundGameCredit/placeDiceBet). findings.title: Countdown lifecycle keeper (cron) targets dead getCountdownStatus/checkAndEndCountdownRound on the new LastSurvivor → automated round settlement silently broken
findings.evidence: platform/host-app/pages/api/cron/miniapp-lifecycle.ts (production handler) calls findCountdownLifecycleApps → platform/host-app/lib/miniapp-lifecycle.ts:126-150 which matches last-survivor via binding 'countdown-auction', resolves contractHash from the runtime module network binding (testnet 0xe238516951 — itself an even-older pre-hardening deploy than the canonical 0x8e1e432e), and derives statusMethod='getCountdownStatus' / maintenanceMethod='checkAndEndCountdownRound' from the stale operations (defaults at lines 45-46 are the same dead names). readCountdownLifecycleState (line 199) invokes getCountdownStatus → RPC fault → empty state → classifyCountdownLifecycle returns start_needed → buildCountdownLifecycleInvoke submits checkAndEndCountdownRound to the relayer → faulting tx. The new contract uses getCurrentRound/currentRoundId (reads) and settle (write) per the live ABI (report safeMethodResults). Mitigant: the lifecycle cron is NOT in vercel.json crons (only miniapp-publish-reminders is) and findCountdownLifecycleApps has no other production caller, so impact is latent unless the endpoint is invoked externally; with finding #1's runtime:{} fix, last-survivor stops matching entirely, so the keeper does nothing for it (FOMO pot never auto-settles via keeper).
findings.fix: Rewire miniapp-lifecycle.ts to the new self-contained LastSurvivor ABI: source the contract from the registry/contracts (canonical 0x8e1e432e), read getCurrentRound/currentRoundId to determine expiry, and submit settle() (no appId arg) as the maintenance invoke. Update DEFAULT_STATUS_METHOD/DEFAULT_MAINTENANCE_METHOD (lines 45-46) and the classify logic to the new round state shape, then re-point findCountdownLifecycleApps to detect last-survivor by app_id rather than the removed runtime binding. Add the cron to vercel.json once validated, or document that settle() is permissionless and relies on player-triggered settlement.
findings.risk: Medium. Keeper submits real on-chain txs via the relayer; wrong wiring could spam faulting txs (gas waste) — gate behind dry_run validation and the existing CRON_SECRET auth. settle() is permissionless so a mis-fire is bounded.

findings.subsystem: apps-ux-quality (apps/* UX + robustness across the 60-miniapp fleet)
findings.title: Indexer-lag event timeout silently misreports success: apps read business data out of result.event with no null branch
findings.evidence: ChainService emits TRANSACTION_UNVERIFIED + sets result.event=undefined when the confirming-event poll times out (apps/shared/services/ChainService.ts:639-646, EVENT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS=45s) — a common case given documented indexer lag. dice-game handles it (apps/dice-game/src/main.tsx:514-522: `if (result.event != null) {...} else statusSettlementPending`), but several apps pull authoritative values straight out of result.event with no guard. apps/dev-tipping/src/composables/useDevTippingWallet.ts:221 `const devId = Number(parseBigInt(eventValue(result.event, 0)))` → devId 0 on timeout; main.tsx:113 returns `result>0` = false to the PlayArea (form not reset, perceived failure) WHILE notify.guard already fired the 'registered' SUCCESS toast (NotificationService.ts:254-255 fires on no-throw) — contradictory UX, and the real on-chain devId is unknown until next refresh. Same class: useDevTippingWallet.ts:259 (withdrawTips reports 0 GAS), :297 (withdrawCredit); apps/memorial-shrine/src/composables/useMemorialShrine.ts:575 emits memorialId=undefined.
findings.fix: In each write that reads from result.event, branch on result.event == null: when null, show the app's 'settlement pending / broadcast, verifying' status (like dice-game's statusSettlementPending) and rely on the post-write reload (loadMemorials/refresh) for the real value, rather than treating the missing event as failure or as a confident success. For dev-tipping specifically, return the action's truth from the refreshed myDeveloperId after refresh() instead of from the event-derived devId, and don't return false when the tx was broadcast. Cleanest systemic fix: add a shared helper (e.g. notify.guardTx) that maps {success, event} → success | pending | failed so all apps render the three states uniformly.
findings.risk: Low blast radius (per-app status wording + return value); reversible. Touches ~6 apps' write handlers.

findings.subsystem: apps-ux-quality (apps/* UX + robustness across the 60-miniapp fleet)
findings.title: DepositConfirmedActionFailedError recovery hint is only wired in ~5 of ~16 deposit-then-act apps
findings.evidence: useContractInteraction/ChainService throw DepositConfirmedActionFailedError when the GAS deposit confirmed on-chain but the consuming call reverted — funds are NOT lost, they sit as withdrawable credit (apps/shared/composables/useContractInteraction.ts:108-124, ChainService.ts:589). Only dice-game, fogplay (useCoinFlip.ts:500), gasbox, quadratic-funding handle this class (grep: 5 files reference it). The other deposit-flow apps with the exact same contract shape (Withdraw(account) credit refund present in MiniAppBreakupPact/BurnLeague/TipJar/TimeCapsule/RedEnvelope/LastSurvivor) do NOT catch it — burn-league, breakup-contract, dev-tipping, graveyard, time-capsule swallow it into a generic 'payment failed' message via notify.error, so a user whose action faulted post-deposit is told it failed and never learns their GAS is recoverable via the withdraw button.
findings.fix: Add a shared error formatter (e.g. NotificationService.error already takes an error — extend it to detect `error instanceof DepositConfirmedActionFailedError` and substitute a 'funds are safe — withdrawable as credit, tap Withdraw to recover or retry' i18n message + surface the withdraw affordance). Apply uniformly so every deposit-then-act app inherits the recovery hint without per-app catch blocks. The withdraw UI already exists in most apps (credit/withdraw-aware: breakup/burn-league/dev-tipping/self-loan/time-capsule/last-survivor/red-envelope), so this is mostly the message + pointing the user at it.
findings.risk: Additive; centralizing in NotificationService.error is one shared edit + i18n keys. Reversible.

findings.evidence: apps/shared/composables/ ships useStatusMessage, useContractInteraction, useWalletBalanceReader specifically to dedupe per-app patterns, yet adoption is: useStatusMessage = 4 apps, useContractInteraction = 9 apps, useWalletBalanceReader = 0 apps (only shared/services/BalanceService.ts imports it). Most apps instead reach for ctx.services.chain (50 apps) + ad-hoc setStatus + bespoke balance reads. The consequence is exactly the divergence seen in the two findings above: the unverified-event handling and the recoverable-credit handling are each correct in some apps and missing in others because there is no single shared write/feedback path everyone goes through.
findings.fix: Pick ChainService (already the de-facto standard at 50 apps) as the one write path and fold the missing concerns into it: (a) a uniform tri-state tx outcome (success/pending/failed) so callers can't misread result.event, (b) DepositConfirmedActionFailedError → recovery-hint mapping. Then deprecate/remove the unused useWalletBalanceReader and the partially-used useStatusMessage/useContractInteraction (or re-point them at ChainService) to kill the dead/duplicate abstraction. This makes the two fixes above land fleet-wide for free.
findings.risk: Moderate — consolidation touches many apps; do it as the carrier for the two higher-severity fixes rather than a standalone refactor.

findings.subsystem: apps-ux-quality (apps/* UX + robustness across the 60-miniapp fleet)
findings.title: registerAction has no built-in re-entrancy lock; double-submit protection is inconsistent across PlayAreas
findings.evidence: Operation buttons dispatch through ctx.registerAction (apps/shared/react/context.ts:142-145) which provides no in-flight guard. Per-app protection is uneven: ~30 composables self-guard with `if (isX.get()) return`, and most primary-action PlayAreas disable their button during processing (on-chain-tarot/breakup-contract/graveyard/time-capsule verified), but coverage is not universal. Practical risk is bounded because ChainService.isProcessing + the wallet's own prompt serialization usually prevent an actual double-spend; the failure mode is a second wallet prompt / duplicate broadcast on apps that neither self-guard nor disable.
findings.fix: Add a single-flight guard inside the action-dispatch layer (wrap each registered handler so a key already in flight returns early and the bound button reads a shared per-key busy flag), making double-submit protection automatic for every app instead of an opt-in each PlayArea must remember.
findings.risk: Low; centralized guard is additive and reversible. Confirm no app relies on overlapping concurrent dispatch of the same key.

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: Gambling games (CoinFlip/DiceGame/GasBox) are drainable via same-transaction abort-on-loss — no anti-contract guard
findings.evidence: MiniAppCoinFlip.cs:132 Flip(), MiniAppDiceGame.cs:143 Roll(), MiniAppGasBox.cs:233 Pull() settle the outcome atomically in the same tx as the bet and only gate on Runtime.CheckWitness(player) (CoinFlip.cs:135, DiceGame.cs:146, GasBox.cs:236). There is NO guard that the caller is the player's own EOA (grep for EntryScriptHash/CallingScriptHash guard returned none). The bet credit is established by OnNEP17Payment (CoinFlip.cs:114-121) which runs in the SAME VM execution as a follow-up Flip call. An attacker deploys a wrapper contract that, in ONE transaction, (1) calls GAS.transfer(attacker→game, amount, "miniapp-fogplay:bet") to credit itself, (2) calls Flip(attacker, choice, amount), (3) inspects the returned outcome and ExecutionEngine.Assert(won) — reverting the ENTIRE atomic invocation on a loss. The attacker's witness is present (it signs the tx), so CheckWitness passes. The contract doc claims 'the outcome is decided in the SAME tx as the wager, so a player cannot see it and abort — there is no abort-and-retry' (CoinFlip.cs:29-32) — this is FALSE for a same-tx wrapper revert. Result: the attacker only ever commits to winning bets, so over time the house bankroll is paid out only on wins and is drained to zero; the 5%/edge math is fully defeated.
findings.fix: Add an anti-composition guard to Flip/Roll/Pull so a contract cannot conditionally revert on the result. Two viable patterns: (a) require the call to originate from a non-contract entry, i.e. assert Runtime.EntryScriptHash == (byte[])player's account is not possible (accounts aren't scripts), so instead require that the player is a standard signer and that ContractManagement.GetContract(Runtime.CallingScriptHash) is null (caller is not a contract) AND Runtime.CallingScriptHash == Runtime.EntryScriptHash; (b) the robust fix — split into commit/reveal across two blocks: bet() records the wager + commit block height in one tx, settle() in a LATER block reads Runtime.GetRandom() at reveal time (the attacker cannot revert a future-block settle they don't control, and cannot predict the future block seed). Given contracts are frozen, this requires a NEW redeploy of CoinFlip, DiceGame, and GasBox plus frontend rewire. Until then, keep house bankrolls minimal (loss is bounded by funded bankroll).
findings.risk: High blast radius: requires redeploying 3 deployed/funded contracts on both nets + frontend rewire + bankroll migration. Option (b) changes UX (two-step play). Reversible (old contracts can be drained-down/abandoned).

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: GetRandom-based games are block-producer biasable AND predictable enough for the house edge to be gamed
findings.evidence: CoinFlip.cs:156, DiceGame.cs:168, GasBox.cs:252, Tarot.cs:126, RedEnvelope.cs:198 all use Runtime.GetRandom() as the sole entropy source for value-bearing outcomes. The contracts' own docs admit 'NOT VRF-grade; a block producer has some influence' (CoinFlip.cs:31). On Neo N3 the per-tx random seed is derived from the block nonce chosen by the consensus primary; a colluding/self-dealing consensus node can bias which transactions land and the nonce, skewing CoinFlip (2 outcomes) and DiceGame (6 outcomes) materially in its own favor. The mixing of player+Runtime.Time+gameId (CoinFlip.cs:158) does NOT add unpredictable entropy — all three are known/controllable by the bettor, so it provides zero protection against a producer. For low-stakes social apps (Tarot/RedEnvelope) this is acceptable, but CoinFlip/DiceGame/GasBox pay real GAS from a house bankroll against this beacon.
findings.fix: For the value-bearing games, move settlement to a commit-reveal across blocks (see prior finding) which both defeats the abort attack and reduces single-block-producer bias, OR integrate the Morpheus VRF oracle for high-value draws (the contracts were originally designed for it). At minimum cap MAX_BET aggressively relative to per-block producer reward so biasing is uneconomic (CoinFlip MAX_BET is currently 100 GAS — DiceGame.cs:53 is 20 GAS, better). Document the trust assumption prominently in the UI. Requires redeploy for any code change.
findings.risk: Same redeploy blast radius as the abort-attack fix; the two should be fixed together. If unaddressed, exposure is bounded by funded bankroll.

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: SelfLoan tier LTV is computed from an owner-set static price with no liquidation — pool is undercollateralizable on NEO appreciation/owner error
findings.evidence: MiniAppSelfLoan.cs:189-200 values collateral as collateral*price where price is a manual owner value (SetNeoPrice, cs:150) with no oracle and no staleness/sanity bound beyond >0. There is no liquidation path and no interest (cs:33-35 acknowledges this). If the owner sets the price too high (fat-finger, or simply because NEO's real GAS value is volatile and the static price drifts above market), a borrower can borrow up to 40% LTV (TIER3, cs:49) of an inflated valuation, walk away, and the pool eats the loss with no recovery mechanism — the only backstop is 'conservative tier LTVs' (cs:35). Because debt==gross and the borrower has zero incentive to repay once disbursed GAS exceeds the real resale value of the locked NEO, the pool is drainable by design under adverse price moves. Pool funds are real GAS owned by NR3E4D8N's contract.
findings.fix: If keeping a static price, (1) add a max price-change rate / bound in SetNeoPrice, (2) lower TIER3 LTV further, (3) keep the pool small. The correct fix is to add a liquidation path: anyone can repay an underwater loan's debt and seize its NEO collateral at a discount once collateralValue*liqThreshold < debt. Needs a NEW redeploy. Lower-effort interim mitigation (no redeploy): owner keeps the pool deliberately small and prices conservatively.
findings.risk: Redeploy + frontend rewire of self-loan; or an off-chain operational mitigation (small pool) with no code change. Pool loss bounded by funded pool.

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: Single hot-key owner (NR3E4D8N, a known testnet WIF) controls all bankrolls/pools on mainnet
findings.evidence: CoinFlip.cs:52, DiceGame.cs:63, SelfLoan.cs:55, Tarot.cs:45, DailyCheckin.cs:67 all hardcode Owner = NR3E4D8NUXh3zhbf5ZkAp3rTxWbQqNih32 via [InitialValue]. Owner-only functions move real funds: WithdrawBankroll (CoinFlip.cs:202, DiceGame.cs:214), WithdrawPool (SelfLoan.cs:159), WithdrawRevenue (Tarot.cs:154, DailyCheckin.Owner.cs:42), SetNeoPrice (SelfLoan.cs:150). Per project memory this WIF is the testnet key, present in .env and transcripts, and it OWNS the mainnet pools — anyone with the WIF can drain WithdrawBankroll/WithdrawPool and (via SetNeoPrice) destabilize SelfLoan. There is no timelock, no multi-sig, no key-rotation method on these contracts.
findings.fix: Rotate ownership to a cold/multi-sig key (the platform already has MiniAppMultisig for custody). Since Owner is a compile-time InitialValue with no setOwner method, rotation requires a NEW redeploy with the new owner baked in, then migrating pool funds. Add a transferOwnership(newOwner) gated by the current owner in the redeployed versions to avoid future redeploys. Immediate operational mitigation: drain mainnet pools to a safe address and refund minimally until rotation.
findings.risk: Redeploy of all owner-bearing contracts + fund migration; or immediate operational drain-to-cold. User has previously accepted this risk per memory, but it remains a live fund-loss exposure.

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: GasBox Pull does not validate machine has TotalWeight>0 before modulo — divide-by-zero / faulted pull is possible but only via a contract path; minor
findings.evidence: MiniAppGasBox.cs:256 computes roll = (entropy+mix) % m.TotalWeight. A machine can only be SetActive(true) when ItemCount>0 (cs:201) and AddItem requires weight>0 (cs:172), so TotalWeight is always >0 for an active machine, and Pull asserts m.Active (cs:240). The path is therefore guarded. Noting it only because the guard is indirect (relies on the SetActive invariant) rather than an explicit assert at the modulo site; a future edit to the activation rules could reintroduce a faulting % 0. Not currently exploitable.
findings.fix: Add an explicit ExecutionEngine.Assert(m.TotalWeight > 0, "no weighted items") immediately before the modulo at GasBox.cs:256 as defense-in-depth. Cosmetic until activation invariants change; not worth a standalone redeploy but fold into any future GasBox redeploy.
findings.risk: None now; defensive only. Would ship with a future redeploy.

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: Modulo bias in dice/gacha/red-envelope draws is real but negligible at current ranges — confirm, do not over-fix
findings.evidence: DiceGame.cs:172 ((entropy+mix) % 6 + 1), GasBox.cs:256 (% TotalWeight), RedEnvelope.cs:202 (% maxShare), Tarot.cs:129 (% remaining) all take a modulo of a large BigInteger derived from GetRandom (a 256-bit value) by a small modulus (≤78, or a weight sum). Modulo bias is bounded by ~modulus/2^256, i.e. astronomically small and undetectable — this is NOT a meaningful unfairness. CoinFlip.cs:160 (% 2) has effectively zero bias. Flagging to CONFIRM this is a non-issue so it isn't mistaken for a bug: the bias here is irrelevant; the actual randomness weakness is GetRandom predictability/bias (separate finding), not the modulo reduction.
findings.fix: No action needed for bias. Do not waste a redeploy on rejection-sampling the modulo — it would add gas cost for no measurable fairness gain. (Documenting to prevent a spurious 'fix'.)
findings.risk: None — recommendation is to NOT change.

findings.subsystem: contracts-safety
findings.title: BurnLeague/GovMerc/LastSurvivor settle reads winner from a single mutable 'top' slot — a late re-burn after a tie can flip the recorded leader vs intent, but accounting stays solvent
findings.evidence: BurnLeague.cs:138-143 tracks only PREFIX_TOP_BURNER/TOP_BURNED and updates on strict > (userTotal > topBurned). Ties never displace the incumbent (correct), and settle pays the recorded top burner the whole pool (cs:176-180) — solvent. LastSurvivor similarly records r.LastBuyer (cs:148) and pays it (cs:177-189) — solvent. GovMerc records high bidder on strict > (cs:231) and distributes the winning bid pro-rata via accRps (Settlement.cs:39); the winner's PREFIX_BID entry is intentionally never deleted and the winner is blocked from reclaim (Settlement.cs:66) — the winning GAS is fully accounted (distributed to stakers) and not strandable. No fund bug. The only sharp edge: these single-slot 'leaders' mean off-chain leaderboards must be rebuilt from events (the contracts say so), and a frontend that trusts only the slot shows a partial board. Not a safety defect.
findings.fix: No on-chain change needed (no solvency/strand issue). Ensure frontends rebuild full leaderboards from Burned/KeysBought/BidPlaced events (the contracts already document this expectation) rather than trusting the single top slot. Verification-only.
findings.risk: None on-chain; frontend-only awareness.

findings.title: 14 self-contained money contracts are immutable (no Update) and have no convention test guarding their security invariants
findings.evidence: None of the 14 migrated contracts contain ContractManagement.Update/Destroy or an Update method (grep across contracts/MiniApp*/*.cs for 'ContractManagement' and 'void Update' returns nothing), so a bug in any live pool/bankroll contract (BurnLeague RewardPool, SelfLoan WithdrawPool, CoinFlip WithdrawBankroll, GovMerc, GasBox) cannot be patched in place — recovery requires deploy-new + fund migration. Meanwhile the source-convention test suites only protect the OLD generation: ContractUpdateCoverageTest.cs:8-11 (admin-gated Update + no-wildcard-token-permission) and ContractSecurityRegressionTest/FinancialTransferSafetyTest target only MiniAppEventTicketPass/Milestone/Quadratic/Soulbound and the Platform* contracts. The 14 self-contained contracts have behavioral TestEngine suites but NO source-convention guard for their critical OnNEP17Payment deposit-then-act invariant — and those behavioral suites explicitly skip the OnNEP17Payment revert path (MiniAppBurnLeagueTests.cs:162-165: the invalid-memo abort 'hangs natively' in TestEngine), the exact pattern that crashed self-loan v1 per project history. So an edit that reintroduces business logic/transfers inside OnNEP17Payment, or adds a wildcard native-token permission, would pass the C# suite.
